findings.claim: The one-column browser fixture conflates 576px with 36rem without pinning the root font size, so the negative assertion can fail or silently pass for the wrong reason.
findings.evidence: Browser fixture: 'Apply an explicit below-576px inline-size constraint to the actual named provider container for the one-column state.' Acceptance: 'assert the computed provider grid has exactly one track below 36rem and exactly two tracks at or above 36rem'. Tailwind container breakpoints are rem-based; 36rem equals 576px only when the document root font-size is 16px, which the plan never asserts or fixes. If the app's root font-size differs (e.g., 14px or 62.5% tricks), a 575px container is at or above 36rem and the 'one track below 36rem' assertion contradicts the fixture.
findings.suggested_fix: Either set/assert `document.documentElement` computed font-size (or fix it to 16px in the fixture) before applying the inline-size constraint, or express the fixture constraint in rem and derive the px value from the measured root font-size at runtime.

findings.claim: The keyboard/focus acceptance clause is under-specified relative to the otherwise concrete grid-track assertions.
findings.evidence: Acceptance: 'Assert document, provider-card, and visible-control overflow bounds; keyboard reachability and visible focus; and preservation of the edited value and modified indicator while crossing the boundary.' No traversal order, expected tabbable element count, or focus-visible selector is named, leaving 'keyboard reachability and visible focus' open to implementer interpretation in the Tier 3 receipt that gates archival.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the assertion mechanically, e.g., 'Tab from the first provider control reaches every visible interactive control without leaving the panel, and the focused element exposes a visible focus indicator (non-zero outline/ring computed style).'
